name: GMAIL Integration
description:
1. **Request:** each codx-junior user must be able to associate their own Gmail account — storing the connection settings and reading/sending email from it.
2. **Findings:** `CodxUser` in `api/codx/junior/model/user.py` is the per-user model, and `GitHubOAuth` already provides a working OAuth precedent; no Gmail/Google code exists yet, so this is greenfield.
3. **Plan:** sliced into 4 deployable, demoable increments — M0 spec/contract, M1 connect & disconnect (identity scopes only, demo 11 Nov), M2 read mail, M3 send & reply, plus M4 admin config in parallel.
4. **Key risk:** Gmail read/send are Google *restricted* scopes, so external users need OAuth verification + a CASA security assessment measured in weeks — internal Workspace users avoid it entirely.
5. **Delivered:** 6 owned tasks on the `External connectors → GMAIL` board, with 5 management decisions (recommended defaults included) and one hard blocker — naming the owner of the Google Cloud project/OAuth client.

I confirmed the key external constraint: Gmail scopes (`gmail.readonly`, `gmail.send`) are Google **restricted** scopes, so any app used by users outside the owning Workspace org needs OAuth app verification plus a CASA security assessment — that is the long-lead item and it drives the plan.

Let me delegate the work to the right profiles on the existing **External connectors → GMAIL** column.All six tasks are on the board. Let me record what I learned about this codebase's extension points so future planning doesn't re-discover it.## #TL; DR;

**Your request:** every codx-junior user must be able to attach their own Gmail account and, from that own account, read and send email. The business outcome is that codx-junior stops being a separate tool you copy emails into, and becomes a place where a user's real mailbox is available.

**What I did:** I looked at how users and settings actually work in this codebase, sliced the feature into 4 increments that each ship and can be shown to management on their own, and put 6 tasks on the existing **External connectors → GMAIL** board with owners and acceptance criteria.

**The one thing you must know:** nothing about "connect an account" is risky — a Google login already fits the pattern used for GitHub in this project. **Reading and sending is the risky part**, because Google classifies mailbox access as *restricted*: for users outside your own Google Workspace organisation, Gmail read/send requires Google's OAuth verification **plus a paid third-party CASA security assessment**, which is measured in **weeks, not days** ([Google OAuth verification](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/9110914)).

> **So the plan is deliberately built so that M1 (connect) works immediately and proves the whole plumbing, while M2/M3 (read/send) can be demoed internally without waiting for Google.** If you want *external* customers reading their own Gmail, that verification is the schedule, and I need decision #1 today.

**Status: on track to start, blocked on one input** — we need the Google OAuth client credentials (decision #4). Everything else has a proposed default and does not need to wait.

---

## 1. Summary

**Request:** a user can associate a Gmail account with their codx-junior user, with all settings needed to connect to Gmail and read/send email from it.

**Business outcome:** user-owned email becomes usable inside codx-junior. Success = a user connects once, then reads and replies to real mail without leaving the product, and can disconnect at any time with the access genuinely revoked.

**What exists today (verified in the code):**
- `CodxUser` (`api/codx/junior/model/user.py`) is the per-user model; per-user sub-objects are added as list fields (`token_limit_rules` is the precedent). Persisted via section files through `global_settings.py`.
- A complete OAuth precedent already exists: `GitHubOAuth` in `api/codx/junior/security/github_oauth.py` (PKCE, state, token exchange) plus `get_oauth_provider()` which already resolves `CODX_{NAME}_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET/_TOKEN_URL`.
- The user-facing place to put this is `client/src/components/security/AccountSettings.vue`; admin provider config lives in `OAuthSettings.vue`.
- **No Gmail or Google code exists yet, and no Google libraries are in `api/pyproject.toml`** — this is greenfield, so the dependency work is part of M1.

## 2. Scope

**In scope (all four increments):** a per-user list of Gmail accounts; secure OAuth connect/disconnect with real revocation; silent token refresh; an "Email accounts" panel in Account settings; reading inbox + message body; sending and replying; admin configuration of the Google OAuth client.

**Out of scope for now:** mailbox mutation (labels, archive, delete, mark read), attachments in/out, multiple simultaneous compose windows, inbox synchronisation / background ingestion, filing email into project knowledge, and non-Gmail providers (IMAP/SMTP). Each of these is a later increment, not a silent addition — say the word and I will size them.

## 3. Increment plan

| # | Milestone | Deliverable | Owner (profile) | Date (forecast) | Deployable? | Demoable? | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | Spec / contract `bb698591` | Model fields, exact scopes per milestone, REST surface, error cases, acceptance criteria | analyst | Tue 3 Nov | n/a | n/a (enables the rest) | todo |
| M1 | **Connect & disconnect** — backend `47517b7d` + front-end `2f481e4e` | Google OAuth, `GmailAccount` on `CodxUser`, encrypted refresh token, `/users/me/gmail/*` endpoints, "Email accounts" panel | py_senior + software_developer; VueDeveloper | dev 4–10 Nov, 1d buffer · **Demo Wed 11 Nov 14:00** | ✅ yes — ships behind a UI flag to internal users | ✅ yes — real account connected in 5 min | todo |
| M2 | **Read mail** `8c6bd455` | `gmail.readonly`, inbox list + message reader, silent refresh, revoked/quota handling | py_senior + VueDeveloper | dev 12–18 Nov · **Demo Thu 19 Nov** | ✅ yes | ✅ yes — real inbox, open a message | todo |
| M3 | **Send & reply** `3b6eb5a0` | `gmail.send`, MIME + threading, compose with confirmation, reply pre-fill | py_senior + VueDeveloper | dev 20–26 Nov · **Demo Fri 27 Nov** | ✅ yes | ✅ yes — send to self, it arrives | todo |
| M4 | **Admin config & hardening** `cfb8ee24` | Google provider in admin settings (env wins), refresh failure/revocation handling, rate limiting, secret handling, deployment + verification doc | py_senior + devops | parallel with M2/M3 · done Fri 27 Nov | ✅ yes | ✅ yes — admin sets credentials, no code change | todo |

All rows say **yes** to deployable and demoable, so no re-slicing is needed. Dates are **forecasts, not commitments** — I have not had the developers confirm them; I will convert M1 to a commitment once they do.

**Deliberate design decision in M1:** it requests only identity scopes (`openid`, `email`, `profile`). That is what lets M1 ship and be demoed **this month without waiting on Google verification**. Mailbox scopes arrive in M2/M3, where the verification gate lives.

## 4. Dependencies & critical path

```
Google Cloud project + OAuth client credentials  ◄── BLOCKS EVERYTHING (decision #4)
                    │
                  M0 spec
                    │
        ┌───────────┴───────────┐
   M1 backend  ─────────►  M1 frontend        (one milestone, two owners, one contract)
        │  ◄── demo 11 Nov, management feedback re-orders the rest
        ├──────────────► M2 read   (+ restricted scope → verification gate)
        └──────────────► M3 send   (+ restricted scope → verification gate)
                    M4 admin config (parallel)
```

- **Contract first:** M1 backend and front-end share the API contract, so M0 must land before either starts. That is why the spec is a task with an owner, not a conversation.
- **Critical path:** credentials → M0 → M1 → M2 → M3. M4 is off the critical path and can absorb slippage.
- **The genuine long pole** is not code: it is Google's restricted-scope verification + CASA assessment, which only gates *external* users. It runs **outside** the team and must be started in parallel on day 1 if external users are in scope.
- **M2 and M3 both change the consent scopes.** Land the scope-upgrade/re-consent handling once, in M2, so M3 does not rework it.

## 5. Risks

| Risk | Impact | Prob. | Mitigation | Owner | Needs decision? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google restricted-scope verification + CASA takes weeks and gates external users | High — M2/M3 unusable by non-org users | High if external | Use **Internal** consent screen now; start verification on day 1; M1 demoes without it | devops + management | **Yes — #1** |
| No Google OAuth client credentials available | High — blocks M1 day 1 | Medium | Management nominates a Google Cloud owner with access now | management | **Yes — #4** |
| Refresh tokens stored in settings files leak | High — full mailbox access | Medium | Encrypt at rest, never serialise into responses or logs, revoke on disconnect, acceptance-tested | py_senior | No |
| Scope creep into "manage my mailbox" (labels, delete, sync) | Medium — pushes M2/M3 past the month | High | Explicit out-of-scope list above; anything new becomes a new increment with a date | ProjectManager | No |
| Expired/revoked token surfaces as a stack trace or silent failure | Medium — looks broken, drives support load | Medium | Explicit account status + "Reconnect" action in M1/M2 acceptance criteria | py_senior | No |
| Accidental double-send on retry | Medium — embarrassing, unrecoverable | Low | No automatic retry; explicit result; button disabled in flight (M3 criteria) | py_senior | No |
| Developers have not confirmed the dates above | Medium — forecast could slip | Medium | Present as forecast; convert to commitment after M1 kickoff | ProjectManager | No |

## 6. Decisions needed from management

1. **Are the users of Gmail read/send inside your own Google Workspace organisation, or external customers?** — *Decide by **Mon 2 Nov** (today).* This decides whether we need Google verification + CASA at all, and therefore whether 27 Nov is realistic.
   - **A (recommended):** internal users only for now — consent screen set to *Internal*, no verification, M2/M3 dates hold; external users become a later, separately-scheduled increment.
   - **B:** external users now — same code, but add a 4–8 week Google verification window before launch, run in parallel from day 1.
   - **Recommendation: A.** It reaches a working read+send increment fastest and keeps the customer promise honest.
2. **Scope policy.** *Decide by **Tue 3 Nov**.* **A (recommended):** least privilege — `gmail.readonly` + `gmail.send`. **B:** `https://mail.google.com/` full access. **Recommendation: A** — B requests far more than read/send needs and makes verification harder and the review scarier.
3. **Who owns the Google Cloud project and its OAuth client?** *Decide by **Tue 3 Nov** — this is the only hard blocker on M1.* We need a named person with admin access who can create the client ID/secret and the redirect URIs per environment. **Recommendation:** devops owns it, management approves the account.
4. **How deep does "read" go?** *Decide by **Thu 12 Nov**.* **A (recommended):** inbox list + message body, read-only. **B:** also labels, search operators, marking read. **Recommendation: A** — B is the single most likely cause of a missed month.
5. **Demo cadence and sign-off.** *Decide by **Tue 3 Nov**.* **A (recommended):** Wednesday 14:00 demo at every milestone boundary, signed off by whoever owns the customer-facing product. **Recommendation: A**, and I need the name of the person who says "done".

## 7. Next demo & checkpoint

**Next demo: Wed 11 Nov, 14:00 — Milestone M1, "Connect a Gmail account".**

What management will see: a real user logging in, clicking *Connect Gmail*, going through Google consent, and returning to Account settings with their address listed — then disconnecting and seeing the grant revoked at Google.

What the team needs to run it: (a) Google OAuth client credentials (decision #3), (b) a real Gmail account to demo with, (c) a staging/demo instance where the client can be deployed. Without (a) I will move the demo rather than fake it.

**Checkpoint immediately before it: Mon 9 Nov** — I will report on track / at risk / off track with M1 explicitly.

## 8. Demo script — M1 (5 minutes, one screen)

| Step | Action | Acceptance criterion demonstrated |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Log in as a normal (non-admin) user, open **Account settings** | The new "Email accounts" section is visible and empty |
| 2 | Click **Connect Gmail** → Google consent screen | Consent asks only for identity (`openid`, `email`, `profile`) — proves M1 needs no restricted-scope approval |
| 3 | Approve, land back on Account settings | Account listed with the real address and a "connected" badge, **no page reload** |
| 4 | Refresh the page | Account persists — it is stored on the user, not in browser state |
| 5 | Inspect the network response for the account list (dev tools, on screen) | **No token value appears** — the security claim, shown rather than stated |
| 6 | Click **Disconnect**, confirm | Account removed; grant gone from the Google account's third-party access page |
| 7 | Log in as a second user | Sees an empty list — accounts are per user, not global |

**Questions for management at the end:** (1) Is this the right place for it — Account settings, or does it belong somewhere more prominent? (2) Given what you just saw, do you confirm Internal-users-only for read/send, or should we start Google verification for external users now? (3) For M2, do you want read-only inbox and reader, or is search also required on day one?

---

**Board:** `External connectors` → column `GMAIL` — tasks `bb698591` (spec), `47517b7d` + `2f481e4e` (M1), `8c6bd455` (M2), `3b6eb5a0` (M3), `cfb8ee24` (M4).

**Next step (one recommendation):** get me the name of the person who owns the Google Cloud project (decision #3). With that in hand I will process the M0 spec task today so M1 can start tomorrow; without it, M1 starts late regardless of how good the plan is.

    -----

      • ``model``    is ``None``  OR  equals the request model

        provider="openai", model="gpt-4o"   # per-model daily cap

import secrets

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

GITHUB_CLIENTS = {}

class GitHubOAuth:
    def __init__(self, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, scope=''):
        self.client_id = client_id
        self.client_secret = client_secret
        self.redirect_uri = redirect_uri
        self.scope = scope
        self.state = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
        self.generate_pkce()
        GITHUB_CLIENTS[self.state] = self

    def generate_pkce(self):
        """Generate code verifier and code challenge for PKCE."""
        # Ensure the code_verifier length is within the required 43 to 128 range by generating more characters
        code_verifier = secrets.token_urlsafe(64)  # Generates a string greater than 43 characters
        hashed = hashlib.sha256(code_verifier.encode()).digest()
        code_challenge = secrets.base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashed).decode().strip('=')
        self.code_challenge = code_challenge
        self.code_verifier = code_verifier

    def get_authorization_url(self, login=None, allow_signup=True, prompt=None):
        """Generate the GitHub authorization URL."""
        params = {
            'client_id': self.client_id,
            'redirect_uri': self.redirect_uri,
            'scope': self.scope,
            'state': self.state,
            'code_challenge': self.code_challenge,
            'code_challenge_method': 'S256',
            'allow_signup': str(allow_signup).lower()
        }
        if login:
            params['login'] = login
        if prompt:
            params['prompt'] = prompt

        auth_url = requests.Request('GET', 'https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize', params=params).prepare().url
        return auth_url

    def get_access_token(self, code):
        """Exchange code for an access token."""
        token_url = 'https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token'
        headers = {
          'Accept': 'application/json'
        }
        data = {
            'client_id': self.client_id,
            'client_secret': self.client_secret,
            'code': code,
            'redirect_uri': self.redirect_uri,
            'code_verifier': self.code_verifier
        }
        logger.info("get_access_token %s", data)
        query_string = "&".join([f"{k}={data[k]}" for k in data.keys()])
        response = requests.post(f"{token_url}?{query_string}", headers=headers)
        try:
            response.raise_for_status()
        except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as err:
            logger.exception("Error requesting github access_token: %s - %s - %s",
                err.request.url,
                str(err),
                err.response.text)
            raise err
        del GITHUB_CLIENTS[self.state]        
        return response.json()

    def get_user_info(self, access_token):
        """Retrieve user information using the access token."""
        headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {access_token}'}
        user_info_url = 'https://api.github.com/user'
        response = requests.get(user_info_url, headers=headers)
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()

MILESTONE 1 (backend half) — a user can connect a real Gmail account and disconnect it. Deployable on its own; nothing waits for reading or sending.

2. api/codx/junior/security/google_oauth.py — a GoogleOAuth client modelled on the existing GitHubOAuth class (PKCE, state handling, authorization url, code->token exchange, token refresh).

   - POST /users/me/gmail/callback — exchange code, store account, store refresh token encrypted
   - DELETE /users/me/gmail/accounts/{id} — revoke at Google and remove locally
4. Refresh-token storage must be encrypted at rest and never serialised into any API response or log.
5. Reuse get_oauth_provider("google") for client_id/secret so it works from settings or CODX_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / CODX_GOOGLE_SECRET.
6. Add the Google deps to api/pyproject.toml (google-auth / google-api-python-client or use direct HTTPS calls — state which and why).

- With a real Google OAuth client in Test/Internal mode, a logged-in user connects a Gmail account and it appears in GET /users/me/gmail/accounts with its address.

- Tokens never appear in response bodies or logs — verified by inspecting the payload.
- DELETE revokes the grant at Google and removes the local record.
- Existing user login and GitHub OAuth still work.

MILESTONE 4 — makes the Gmail capability operable by an admin and safe to run for more than one user. Depends on M1; can run in parallel with M2/M3.

Profiles chosen: py_senior (settings model + provider resolution + hardening) and devops (deployment/env var wiring, secret handling, verification readiness).

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. Expose Google as an OAuth provider in global settings: register the provider so get_oauth_provider("google") resolves from the settings file as well as from CODX_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / CODX_GOOGLE_SECRET, and surface it in the existing admin OAuth settings UI (client/src/components/oauth_settings/OAuthSettings.vue) without breaking the GitHub entry.
2. Handling for: token refresh failure, revoked grant, per-user rate limiting, and surfacing GmailAccount.last_error to the owner.
3. Document and implement secret handling: refresh tokens encrypted at rest, client secret only from env/settings, never in logs or git.
4. Deployment doc: how to create the Google Cloud project, which consent-screen user type (Internal vs External) is used, redirect URIs per environment, and what is required before real users outside the org can connect (restricted-scope verification + CASA assessment).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- An admin can configure the Google client id/secret from the admin settings UI, and the user-facing connect flow picks it up without a code change.
- Env-var configuration still wins over the settings file (existing convention preserved).
- A revoked or expired token is detected and shown to the user as a reconnect prompt; the failure is recorded in last_error.
- The deployment doc states plainly what must be done before non-org users can use Gmail read/send.

# User settings & external connector extension points

Where to plug a per-user external account (e.g. Gmail) into codx-junior.

## User model & persistence
- `CodxUser` is a pydantic model in `api/codx/junior/model/user.py`.
- Per-user sub-models are plain pydantic classes added as list fields on `CodxUser`
  (precedent: `token_limit_rules`, `token_limit_requests`).
- Persistence goes through `api/codx/junior/global_settings.py`, which stores each
  `GlobalSettings` field as its own section file via `GlobalSettingsManager`.
  Use `write_settings_section(section, data)` for partial updates.
- Security logic lives in `api/codx/junior/security/user_management.py`
  (`UserSecurityManager`, `get_authenticated_user`).

## OAuth
- Working precedent: `api/codx/junior/security/github_oauth.py` — `GitHubOAuth` class
  with PKCE (`generate_pkce`), state registry (`GITHUB_CLIENTS[state]`),
  `get_authorization_url()`, `get_access_token(code)`, `get_user_info(token)`.
- Provider config resolution: `get_oauth_provider(name)` in `global_settings.py`.
  Resolution order: env vars first (`CODX_{NAME}_CLIENT_ID`, `CODX_{NAME}_SECRET`,
  `CODX_{NAME}_TOKEN_URL`), then the `oauth_providers` settings section.
- Login routes are in `api/codx/junior/api/users.py`
  (`/users/oauth-login-url/{provider}`, `/users/oauth-login`).

## Front-end
- Per-user account UI: `client/src/components/security/AccountSettings.vue`
  (Vue 3, daisyUI classes, `$user`, `$users`, `$toast` globals).
- Admin OAuth provider UI: `client/src/components/oauth_settings/OAuthSettings.vue`.
- Client API modules: `client/src/api/modules/*.js`, user store `client/src/store/users.js`.

## Conventions worth keeping
- Tokens/secrets must never be serialised into API responses or written to logs.
- Consent-scope growth forces re-consent: request the minimal scope per increment and
  handle "account connected but missing scope" explicitly instead of failing silently.

## Kanban
- External integrations live on board `External connectors`
  (existing columns: `WhatsApp`, `GMAIL`).
